findings.summary: submit_pass re-implements the batch submission the repository already owns: reckon/crew/fleet_node.py:289 runs sbatch --parsable with the script on stdin, returns the job id and raises on refusal, and reckon/crew/landing_measure.py:755 partition_submission declares itself the one batch submission form every partitioned measure uses, built there and nowhere else. The new helper duplicates that capability behind an added --partition argv seam instead of extending either owner.

assert stored['threshold'] == threshold compares the record against a second call to the same function (maintenance.automatic_threshold at line 109) rather than the fixture's independently declared THRESHOLD=100, so it stays green whatever that function returns, including the 6700 fallback.

The production wiring that constructs MaintenanceSweep is uncovered: the three schedule tests inject their own sweep and the slow-station driver patches MaintenanceSweep.run to a no-op, so deleting the construction here would leave the suite green while the schedule silently stopped.

The node embeds a figure (docs/figures/work-flows-to-the-lane/wftl-a-managed-repository-is-kept-packed/maintenance-counts.svg) that its done-when does not name; the dispatch contract permits no figure beyond the landing fragment unless the done-when names that artifact. A separate figure review record already carries two non-blocking findings on the same file.
